Booty
bōō´tĭ
n. (plunder taken in war; rendering Hebrew baz and malqoach)
From Old Norse byti, exchange or share. Booty is captured goods divided among captors — and Scripture regulates the division carefully.

Biblical Definition

Booty is plunder. Moses divides the Midianite spoil between those who went to battle and the whole congregation, with a tribute levied for the LORD (Num 31:27,32). Jeremiah promises the faithful Ethiopian Ebedmelech, “thy life shall be for a prey unto thee” (Jer 39:18). Habakkuk asks whether the Chaldean shall “empty his net, and not spare continually to slay the nations” (Hab 1:17), and Zephaniah says the remnant shall take the booty of the proud (Zep 2:9).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines booty as spoil taken from an enemy in war; plunder; pillage; and that which is seized by violence and robbery.

expand to see more

BOOTY, n. Spoil taken from an enemy in war; plunder; pillage.

2. That which is seized by violence and robbery.

Key Scripture

Num 31:27 — "And divide the prey into two parts; between them that took the war upon them, who went out to battle, and between all the congregation:"

Jer 39:18 — "For I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey unto thee: because thou hast put thy trust in me, saith the LORD."

Zep 2:9 — "Therefore as I live, saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them."

Hab 1:17 — "Shall they therefore empty their net, and not spare continually to slay the nations?"

Modern Corruption

Reward is claimed by whoever did the visible work, and Israel's spoil law divided it between the men who fought and the congregation who stayed.

expand to see more

Numbers 31:27 legislates a division that soldiers would not have chosen: divide the prey into two parts; between them that took the war upon them, who went out to battle, and between all the congregation. The men who risked their lives received half; the people who stayed home received the other half. David later makes the same ruling permanent after Ziklag — as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff.

The principle protects a community from being sorted into heroes and dependants. Those who go and those who hold the ground both share, because the enterprise belonged to all of them. Applied to a church, it means the visible worker and the quiet supporter are on the same ledger, which is roughly what Paul says about the body's less honourable members receiving more abundant honour.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew baz (H957), spoil, booty; malqoach (H4455), prey taken; shalal (H7998), spoil.

expand to see more

Hebrew malqoach (H4455) — booty, prey; Numbers 31:11-12, 26-27, 32.

Hebrew baz (H957) — spoil, booty; Zephaniah 2:9, Isaiah 10:6.

Hebrew shalal (H7998) — spoil, prey; Jeremiah 39:18, thy life shall be for a prey.

Usage

"“Divide the prey… between them that took the war… and… all the congregation” — a division soldiers would not have chosen."

"“Thy life shall be for a prey unto thee” — the reward promised to a faithful foreigner."

"“The residue of my people shall… possess them” — Zephaniah's reversal."
